skill.name: documentation-writer
skill.description: Creates and updates documentation for the Logseq Template Graph project, including module READMEs, user guides, technical references, and API documentation.
skill.summary: Create clear Logseq Template Graph documentation from source files, templates, and existing guides.
skill.author: C0ntr0lledCha0s

security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives caused by Markdown fences, template text, relative documentation links, and a Schema.org reference URL. No prompt injection, exfiltration intent, or malicious code was found. One contextual risk remains: the skill encourages Bash command testing without explicit approval safeguards.

remediation.issue: Bash command testing can execute unsafe repository-provided commands.
remediation.suggestion: Require user approval before running commands, and restrict testing to non-destructive commands in a controlled environment.

semantic_findings.title: Unbounded Shell Command Testing Guidance
semantic_findings.description: The skill tells agents to use Bash and to run all commands before documenting them. Without an explicit approval or safety rule, this can execute repository-provided commands during documentation work.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited lines explicitly list Bash as a tool for testing commands and say to run all commands. The risk is contextual because the commands may be benign, but repository-controlled examples could be unsafe.

content.value_statement: Project documentation often becomes incomplete, inconsistent, or hard to maintain. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code draft structured guides, READMEs, and references from project files.
actual_capabilities: Creates module README outlines with overview, classes, properties, examples, and Schema.org mapping.
Drafts user guides with prerequisites, steps, examples, troubleshooting, and FAQ sections.
Produces technical references for components, dependencies, interfaces, parameters, and return values.
Documents commands with syntax, options, expected output, exit codes, and related references.
Reviews source files, scripts, and templates to extract details for accurate documentation.
Applies a quality checklist for accuracy, formatting, links, examples, and indexes.
limitations: The guidance is tailored to the Logseq Template Graph project and may need adaptation for other repositories.
Accurate output depends on access to current source files, templates, and existing documentation.
Command testing guidance requires human approval before running shell commands.
It cannot guarantee link status or command safety without separate validation.

use_cases.title: Document a New Module
use_cases.description: Create a module README from source files with class summaries, property details, examples, and related links.

use_cases.title: Update a User Guide
use_cases.description: Revise an installation or workflow guide while preserving structure, terminology, examples, and troubleshooting sections.

use_cases.title: Create an API Reference
use_cases.description: Turn script or command details into a reference with syntax, options, output behavior, and exit code notes.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Module README
prompt_templates.prompt: Write a README for the person module. Use the existing source files and include overview, classes, properties, examples, and related modules.

prompt_templates.title: Improve a Guide
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for an existing document.
prompt_templates.prompt: Update the installation guide with the latest steps. Keep the current structure and add troubleshooting for common setup errors.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Technical Reference
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a technical reference for the build script. Explain purpose, dependencies, parameters, outputs, examples, and exit codes.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Documentation Quality
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these documentation files for accuracy, missing prerequisites, outdated links, unclear examples, and inconsistent terminology. Return prioritized fixes.

output: A module README with a short overview and scope.
Class and property sections based on the module source files.
Practical usage examples and Schema.org references.

output_examples.input: Update the installation guide with new setup steps.
output: A revised guide with prerequisites, ordered steps, examples, and troubleshooting.
Existing headings and style preserved where possible.
A checklist of commands, links, and terms that need validation.

output_examples.input: Create documentation for a project command.
output: A command reference with purpose, syntax, options, outputs, and exit codes.
Examples for common usage and notes for related commands.

best_practices: Provide the relevant source files and current documentation before asking for a draft.
Review generated examples and commands before publishing them.
Ask for a final checklist covering accuracy, links, formatting, and missing sections.
anti_patterns: Do not publish generated documentation without checking source accuracy.
Do not ask the skill to invent missing APIs, files, or command behavior.
Do not run generated or discovered shell commands without approval and context.

faq.question: What documentation can this skill create?
faq.answer: It can create module READMEs, user guides, technical references, API documentation, and quality checklists.

faq.question: Is this skill only for Logseq Template Graph?
faq.answer: It is written for that project, but its documentation structures can be adapted to similar repositories.

faq.question: Does it read source files?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill instructs the agent to read source files, scripts, templates, and existing documentation for accuracy.

faq.question: Can it update existing documentation?
faq.answer: Yes. It can revise guides while preserving structure, style, terminology, and related references.

faq.question: Does it execute commands automatically?
faq.answer: The skill recommends command testing, but users should require approval before any shell command runs.

faq.question: What should users review before publishing?
faq.answer: Users should verify examples, commands, links, terminology, prerequisites, and coverage of important features.
